recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant prose for FHIR-3527; any future change to default or missing-element semantics should be handled as separate FHIR-I/MnM work.
issue_request: FHIR-3527 asked MnM to make explicit that FHIR elements, including optional booleans, do not have implicit defaults, and that boolean values that must always be known should be mandatory with a required primitive value.
initial_application: Jira records SVN revision 3486 as the initial application, but no converted Git commit in this checkout mentions FHIR-3527 or revision 3486. Later Git history shows the current policy being completed by commits 72143f2 and 7ac081b, which removed default-value examples and residual default prose.
additional_context: FHIR-15121 and the January 2018 FHIR-I minutes later refined the policy by removing defaultValue[x] for FHIR resources/datatypes, retaining meaningWhenMissing only for explicit missing semantics, and treating extension-only primitives as missing. Current source reflects that later policy.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/elementdefinition.html already states missing elements generally mean unknown, extension-only primitives count as missing, explicit missing meanings are listed, and resources/datatypes define no defaults. source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml and source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-StructureDefinition.xml encode and enforce the same rule.

related_jiras.note: Published FHIR-I grouper that refined the current defaultValue[x]/meaningWhenMissing policy and explains the current source state.
